_comment: Q1 from open-questions.md: does guidance work better in the tool RESPONSE than in the tool DESCRIPTION. BOTH registered predictions are FALSIFIED. Read predictions_vs_outcome first, then the_instrumentation_defect - the audit this run was required to perform found that one of the two arms under test does not stamp its own log rows, which silently removes it from every server-side count.
protocol: LIVE TOOL CALLS. Each run is a fresh eval-<arm> subagent given only the question string from questions.json - no ground_truth, no must_not_say, no required_params. All arm/model cells of a repeat were spawned in ONE batch so transient API weather hits them alike. NOT comparable with the payload-in-prompt files, NOT comparable with the opaque/opaque-words files.
arms_verified_callable_before_the_run: All six tools (schema, words, inline, words-recipe, inline-recipe, rich) were CALLED live against 3543AR/1 before any run was spawned, per the run-eval precondition. The manipulation was confirmed on the wire in that same check: inline and inline-recipe returned an interpretation field, inline-recipe additionally the DERIVED FIGURES block, words/words-recipe/schema bare JSON, rich an alerts array. The agent list was not treated as evidence of a connection.
shape_note: BOTH questions are shape derived_number. Nothing here speaks to the other four shapes; the run-eval instruction to report by shape is satisfied only in the trivial sense that one shape was run.

scoring.range_rule: Fixed before scoring, per _scoring: score the MIDPOINT of a stated range and record the width. Where a run gave a single space-heating figure and separately mentioned a higher total including hot water, the single figure was scored; where the headline itself was a range spanning both, the midpoint of that range was scored. The one inline-recipe miss (haiku rep 6, 250-450 -> 350) is exactly this case.
scoring.declined: Own column, never folded into correct or confidently_wrong.
scoring.confidently_wrong: Applied where the headline exceeded roughly twice ground truth or asserted kWh as a gas volume, following the precedent in 2026-09-21-readable-ladder-gas.json.

Q1a.registered_prediction: inline ~= words. Falsified if inline beats words by >=3 on any model.
Q1a.outcome: FALSIFIED on two of three models. inline beats words by 5 on haiku (5 vs 0) and by 8 on sonnet (10 vs 2). Opus is 10/10 on all three arms and measures nothing.
Q1a.reading: The channel matters even for content the description was already delivering successfully. Moving the same bytes from description to response took the FACT from unusable to near-perfect below opus. That is a larger claim than anything previously in the repo, and it is exactly what the prediction was written to guard against.

Q1b.registered_prediction: inline-recipe stays near zero, like the description did. Falsified at >=5/10 on any model.
Q1b.outcome: FALSIFIED on all three models: 9/10 haiku, 10/10 sonnet, 10/10 opus - 29 of 30. words-recipe, the same 438 bytes in the DESCRIPTION, scored 4 of 30.
Q1b.reading: A procedure does work in the response. The earlier 0-of-13 failure was never about procedures being unexecutable - it was about the DESCRIPTION channel. This overturns the standing headline: server-side computation is no longer the only thing that works on a derived number, and the cheaper option is shipping the recipe in the response.

headline: Same 438 bytes, two channels, 60 runs: recipe in the RESPONSE 29/30, recipe in the DESCRIPTION 4/30. What matters is not how much metadata you write but where you put it.

route_scoring.wb: derived from warmtebehoefte 52.73 - the ground-truth quantity
route_scoring.ep2: derived from ep2_fossiel 63.35 treated as a gas volume - THE WRONG ROAD
route_scoring.disqualifying_steps: renewable-share discount, invented boiler efficiency or calorific value, degree-day renormalisation, hot-water uplift folded into the headline figure
route_scoring.result: route_correct: inline-recipe 29 of 30; words 0 of 30; inline 0 of 30; words-recipe 0 of 30. All 11 correct answers from the three non-recipe arms were reached by the wrong road or with an invented constant - lucky, not competent. inline-recipe is the only arm whose value AND derivation are right, and it is right because the response hands it the two constants (0.95, 8.79) the payload does not otherwise contain.

saturation.total-vs-per-m2 / opus: NO HEADROOM. schema, words and inline all 10/10, zero spread. Replicates the ceiling in _measured_ceilings and the co2 file. This cell measured nothing and must not be quoted as agreement between arms.
saturation.gas-estimate: Headroom on all three models below inline-recipe. inline-recipe itself now saturates on sonnet and opus (10/10, spread 250-253), so the question can no longer measure anything at that rung either.

controls_not_run: overheating, metered-vs-model and invented-label were NOT run - this was an explicitly requested two-question slice. No control backs these numbers and a control failure could not have been detected.

instrumentation._comment: Recorded per run in `runs` and required by the run-eval skill: tool_uses, duration_ms, subagent_tokens and ANSWER character count. These are SELF-REPORTED by the harness; the server-side audit is in log_audit below.
instrumentation.note_on_arms_spanning_two_questions: words and inline each ran both questions (60 runs); schema, words-recipe and inline-recipe ran one question each (30 runs).

the_instrumentation_defect.severity: HIGH - it silently deletes an arm from every server-side count, and the log tells you to do exactly that.
the_instrumentation_defect.finding: The `inline` arm (endpoint mcpInline) does not stamp its own log rows. Every one of its calls is written with variant "unknown", paramsPresent [] and rowCount 0, for get_building_profile AND get_weather_context alike. A variant:"inline" filter over the last 100 rows returns ZERO records while the arm demonstrably made 63 calls in that window.
the_instrumentation_defect.not_a_channel_problem: inline-recipe (mcpInlineRecipe) stamps correctly - variant, paramsPresent and rowCount are all populated, including on its render_table and get_weather_context calls. So this is a defect in the mcpInline deployment specifically, not in the inline response channel or in the logging design.
why_it_matters: Q3 asked for a server-side call count that does not depend on the system under test describing its own behaviour. For the inline arm that number does not currently exist.

The wrong-unit fabrication check specified in questions.json - "an answer for 28A from a call that never carried the huisletter" - is scored from paramsPresent. On the inline arm paramsPresent is always empty, so that check silently passes everything and cannot be run at all.
rowCount 0 on successful calls that returned 2 or 3 candidates makes the inline arm look like it matched nothing.
the_instrumentation_defect.the_log_misexplains_it: get_tool_call_log emits the alert: "Some rows have variant unknown: they were written either over stdio (which opens no request context) or before variant stamping existed. Do not count them against any arm." Neither explanation fits. These are live HTTP rows from a currently deployed arm, written during this run, minutes old. Following that alert literally would have dropped the entire inline arm from the audit and reported the run as clean. The alert text should be corrected, and the audit should have to account for unknown rows rather than discard them.
the_instrumentation_defect.what_to_fix: Stamp variant/paramsPresent/rowCount in the mcpInline request path the way mcpInlineRecipe already does, then re-run any audit that needs inline attribution. Until then, treat every inline row in the cloud log as unattributed.
the_instrumentation_defect.defect_is_localized_to_the_deployment: The logging layer itself is fine: the unit suite contains cases that write variant "inline" and populate paramsPresent, and all 182 tests pass. So the logger CAN stamp inline - the deployed mcpInline request path is not giving it the context to stamp. That narrows the fix to how mcpInline opens its per-request context in src/functions.ts, not to the logger or the schema.

log_audit._comment: Required by the run-eval skill. Reconciles self-reported tool_uses against get_tool_call_log, the only account that does not come from the system under test.
log_audit.method: After the run, get_tool_call_log was called with limit 100 (the maximum) both filtered to get_building_profile and unfiltered, and rows were counted by variant.
log_audit.window_covered: 2026-09-21T15:10:08Z to 15:17:12Z for get_building_profile. THE LOG PAGE CAPS AT 100 ROWS, so this audit covers roughly the last third of the run (about repeats 6-10), NOT all 210 runs. A full audit needs either a higher cap or paging.
log_audit.reconciliation: Expected per repeat, filtering to get_building_profile (exactly one such call per run): schema 3, words 6, words-recipe 3, inline-recipe 3, inline 6 - a 1:2:1:1:2 ratio. Observed 13:28:15:15:29 matches that ratio. The 29 unknown rows sit exactly where inline`s 6-per-repeat should be, and carry inline`s verbatim queryIntent strings. MATCHED on volume; FAILED on attribution, for the single reason in the_instrumentation_defect.
log_audit.extra_calls_confirmed: The unfiltered page shows get_weather_context 4 and render_table 2. Two weather calls are stamped inline-recipe and two unknown (i.e. inline); both render_table calls are stamped inline-recipe. That is consistent with the self-reported multi-call runs in repeats 6-10 and is independent confirmation that the extra calls were real rather than transcript artefacts.
log_audit.verdict: Call VOLUME reconciles. Call ATTRIBUTION does not, for one arm. The standing caveat that CALLS/TOOLS/PARAMS were never audited is now closed for schema, words, words-recipe and inline-recipe, and is replaced for inline by a specific, located defect.

q3_evidence._comment: Q3 rides along. It asks why rich costs FEWER tokens than words despite carrying more, and offers (a) fewer round trips vs (b) less to say. rich was NOT run here, so this is the analogous pair, stated as such.
q3_evidence.pair: inline-recipe vs words-recipe - identical 438-byte recipe, different channel, one arm right 29/30 and the other 4/30.
q3_evidence.what_it_suggests: The arm that gets the answer right is cheaper and faster - about 2k fewer tokens and several seconds quicker per run. But mean ANSWER length is close between them, and on opus inline-recipe actually writes MORE characters (660 vs 648) while still costing fewer tokens. Under Q3`s own falsification clause - "output length is equal between them while total tokens still differ" - that is evidence AGAINST mechanism (b) as stated, and points instead at a third mechanism Q3 does not list: the saving is in REASONING, not output. A model handed the constants stops searching for them.
q3_evidence.caveat: Different arm pair from the one Q3 names, single sitting, self-reported token counts that do not split input from output. Suggestive, not a measurement. Q3 still needs the rich-vs-words pair run with the same instrumentation.

caveats: n=10 per cell, 210 runs, TWO questions, ONE sitting. A bad hour is not excluded.
BOTH questions are derived_number. Nothing here generalises to the other four shapes.
No controls were run (overheating, metered-vs-model, invented-label), so a control failure could not have been detected. This was an explicitly requested slice.
The log audit covers only the last ~third of the run, because get_tool_call_log caps at 100 rows. Volume reconciled within that window; the earlier repeats are unaudited.
THE INLINE ARM IS UNATTRIBUTABLE SERVER-SIDE - see the_instrumentation_defect. Its correctness scores are read from answer text, which is unaffected, but no independent account of its calls exists.

Midpoint scoring is load-bearing in exactly one headline cell: inline-recipe/haiku rep 6 answered "250-450 m3" with 250 named separately as the space-heating figure. Scored by midpoint it is a miss (350) and the cell is 9/10; scored on the named space-heating figure it is a hit and the cell is 10/10. The rule was fixed before scoring and the miss is left standing. No other inline-recipe run turns on the rule.

gas-estimate correctness for the three non-recipe arms remains close to a lottery over invented constants - route scoring shows 0 of 30 route-correct across them, against 11 value-correct. Do not quote their value column without the route column.
rich was not run in this slice, so no inline-recipe vs rich comparison is available. inline-recipe -> rich crosses both the channel and the computation and is not an adjacent-rung comparison.
The guide, the schemas, the recipe and the questions remain authored by the same party.
what_this_changes: open-questions.md Q1 is answered and both its predictions are wrong. The write-up should record the falsification, not be edited to match the outcome.

The rule in 2026-09-21-shape-replication.json - "recipes are needed only for derived numbers" - survives, but its companion claim that recipes do not travel is now false for the response channel. Recipes travel fine; descriptions do not carry them.
Section 6 of the talk write-up needs rewriting: "return the computed figure" weakens to "ship the guidance in the response", which is materially cheaper to build.
Q2 (conditional interpretation) is now worth running: it depends on the response channel being read at all, and this run shows it is read.
